KEY MESSAGE 1...Rip current risk continues along the east coastal 
areas into this evening.

Swell energy coming in from the east has been resulting in rip
currents along primarily east facing beaches today. This energy 
will slowly be diminishing this evening and overnight. As that 
happens, the risk for rip currents along primarily east facing 
beaches will also slowly diminish. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Small chance of a shower or thunderstorm through 
this evening across the interior, otherwise tranquil weather 
through Wednesday night.

Although it's taken awhile, much of the low clouds across the
eastern half of southern New England have finally started to
lift and break up. Satellite imagery shows daytime cumulus
developing across the interior thanks to relatively abundant low
level moisture. However the latest mesoanalysis does not show
much mixed layer CAPE and still some CIN due to a weak inversion
aloft. Although a shower or isolated brief thundershower is
possible, the chances are pretty low. Did maintain continuity
with previous forecasts and painted in a roughly 20% chance,
mainly across the Worcester Hills into NE CT and northern RI.
This is where the thermal gradient (due to slightly cooler
temperatures where the low clouds hung around longest and where
more sunshine has developed) will also be maximized. Otherwise,
the next 36 hours will be dry for the vast majority of the
region. Could be another round of low clouds and some fog across
southeast MA/Cape/Islands late tonight due to the still somewhat
humid airmass. Otherwise models are all consistent with dry
weather tomorrow. With plenty of sun and 925mb temperatures
around 20C, we should see surface temperatures either side of
30C (ie: mid 80s F). Stuck with model blend for that reason.
Quiet and seasonable conditions continue Wednesday night. 


KEY MESSAGE 3...Unsettled weather returns Thursday with high 
pressure and pleasant weather following for Friday

Guidance continues to show a shortwave moving east towards the CWA 
on zonal flow Thursday. Aloft, the jet stream becomes cyclonically 
curved placing our region under the jet's left exit region. These 
mid and upper level dynamics provide ample forcing for 
precipitation. The caveat here will be dry low and mid level 
moisture profiles across much of the region. Thus, expecting mainly 
light showers across the southern portion of the CWA with mostly 
cloudy skies elsewhere. Still, there are some discrepancies within 
guidance suites. Namely, the global models, including the NBM, show 
a drier solution with probs of QPF exceeding 0.25" less than 30%. In 
contrast, CAMs show a more amplified, moisture-rich wave with 
locally heavy rain and a low risk for thunderstorms. Think the 
solution lies somewhere in between the two extremes with scattered 
showers possible mainly along and S of the Mass Pike Thursday 
afternoon and evening. 

The frontal wave passes E of the region late Thursday. Dew point 
temperatures crash into the upper 50s Friday as high pressure builds 
overhead. Temperatures will likely be in the low 80s and down to the 
mid 70s, particularly along the coasts where onshore winds will keep 
it slightly cooler. 


KEY MESSAGE 4...Another round of unsettled weather possible for
the second half of the weekend. 

Guidance shows an even larger shortwave arriving from the Great 
Lakes later Saturday with plenty of upper-level energy. Behind the 
lead shortwave, a series of shortwaves moving along the boundary 
that may stall just off the east coast could bring chances for 
showers. Thunderstorms could be a possibility depending on if these 
waves could take advantage of daytime heat. More details will become 
apparent as we approach this timeframe. At the moment, guidance 
blends show a 30-50% chance of rain through much of the interior and 
60-70% along the coast from Saturday night to Monday morning.
